title: Constructing a Category
summary: Turn six messy accounts of daily life into a named condition: select its features, name it, set a threshold, and write a screening questionnaire. Then decide who gets to use it.
learningObjectives: Identify the specific steps at which a classification acquires the appearance of a naturally given object.
Explain why a prevalence figure is manufactured by a threshold rather than discovered.
Describe what a category name imports before any evidence has been collected.
Recognise criterion contamination, where an instrument restates the criteria it is supposed to test.
State why social construction is not fabrication, and what a critical realist adds to that distinction.
interactionTypes: threshold slider on a simulated population
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; the questionnaire is never administered to the person using the tool, and every calculation runs in the browser tab.
accessibilityNotes: Native checkboxes, radios, a range and two selects; no dragging and no timing. The five stages expose only their own controls and their own result, which keeps the controls column short enough for the pinned result to stay in view at 1366x768. Both bar charts are hidden from assistive technology and paired with visible tables or with counts printed beside every bar, so no band is identified by fill alone; the object-status index is stated in words as well as drawn. Feature counts are printed next to each checkbox so no judgement requires reading the table. Focus moves to the new stage heading when a stage button is pressed. Changes are announced through the shell's polite live region; reduced motion honoured; forced-colours rules provided; usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths. The category under construction is pinned as a definition list at the top of the stage area and gains a row as each stage is reached, so the running state is available as text throughout rather than only inside the stage that produced it. Controls held back for a second pass sit inside native <details> elements, so they are reachable by keyboard in one step and are announced as collapsed rather than being disabled.
readmeTopic: From six accounts to a named condition with a prevalence figure: reification broken into steps you can point at
simulationNotes: The six accounts, the twelve candidate features, the comparison counts (authored against a comparison set of the same size), the five candidate names, the ten questionnaire items and the five institutional events are all authored for teaching; no published category, criteria set, instrument, item or prevalence estimate is reproduced or referred to. Stage 3 uses 400 simulated respondents generated from a seeded mulberry32 generator (seed 20260807) with Box-Muller normal draws: each respondent has a latent load, feature f is present when a uniform draw falls below logistic(intercept_f + slope_f x latent), and duration in months and an interference score are separate draws containing the same latent. A respondent meets the criteria when the number of selected features present reaches the threshold and the duration and interference requirements are met. With the worked-example feature set the prevalence runs 41.3, 37.8, 28.0, 17.3, 7.0 and 0.0 per cent across thresholds one to six, with the population held completely fixed. Stage 4 detects an account when it would endorse three or more of the five chosen items; accounts 3 and 6 are written so that the five most obvious items miss them. Stage 5 offers two of its five institutional decisions on first sight and the other three behind a disclosure; all five carry the same deltas, so the route a learner takes through them does not change the arithmetic. The stage 5 object-status index runs from 12 to 100 and is a teaching device, not a measurement.
